sections.h2: Where do I go in Danielsville with a Madison County tax question?
sections.html:
Everything runs out of the Government Complex at 91 Albany Avenue, the former Danielsville Elementary School building that the county renovated and moved into in June 1997. Property Valuation sits upstairs in Suite 404 and speaks for the Board of Assessors. The Tax Commissioner is in Suite 14.

The split is simple. If the complaint is about what the house is worth, how many acres the record shows, or an exemption that never appeared, call Property Valuation. If the question is how much is owed or whether a check cleared, call the Tax Commissioner. Parcel records can also be searched at qpublic.net/ga/madison.

A drop box at the back of the complex takes payments after hours. The county says this one office is the lone place for property, mobile home and timber tax billing.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Madison County for a home seller?
sections.html:
Think of it as Athens' quiet neighbor to the northeast. The county government describes itself as minutes from Athens, Commerce and Elberton, with parades in Colbert, a fall festival in Danielsville and a Christmas parade in Comer. Carlton, Colbert, Comer, Danielsville, Hull and Ila are the six towns.

The county was carved out in 1811 as Georgia's 38th and takes its name from President James Madison. Danielsville was named for General Allen Daniel and made the seat in 1812. Crawford W. Long, the first doctor to use ether in surgery, was born there in 1815, and his boyhood home is on the National Register of Historic Places. Cotton wore out much of the soil before the 1930s, and the county now counts about 23 percent of its acreage as prime farmland, with chickens and eggs leading agribusiness.

  • Residents: 32,919 in the July 2025 estimate, a 9.3 percent rise over the April 2020 base.
  • Space: 282.32 square miles of land, or 106.7 people per square mile in 2020.
  • Tenure: 76.9 percent of the 11,242 households own their home.
  • Prices: owner-occupied homes had a median value of $219,700, and rent ran $972 a month.
  • Earnings: households took in $61,963 at the median, and the average worker spent 29.5 minutes getting to a job.
  • New construction: the county logged 130 building permits in 2025.

All of those numbers are Census Bureau QuickFacts.

sections.h2: How is a Madison County house appraised?
sections.html:
Georgia taxes 40 percent of fair market value, and the figure is fixed as of January 1. Madison County's appraisers use sales of similar parcels, replacement cost less depreciation plus land, and an income method for rentals and commercial space.

Notices arrive between April and May. Treat one as a preview, because it shows the appraised value that will drive the later bill. Owners who want to sell in the spring market should open it right away, since the clock for objecting starts on the notice date.

Returns are filed with Property Valuation from January 1 through April 1. One return is enough until something changes, such as a new garage, an added acre or a wish to declare a different value.

  • Field appraisers measure buildings and take photos. They show photo identification and drive marked county vehicles.
  • Specialized assessments, including conservation use, have to be applied for by April 1.
  • The county says it honors only a U.S. Postal Service postmark on returns, homestead forms and appeals.

sections.h2: What are the billing dates in Madison County?
sections.html:
Most owners see a bill in September with a normal due date of December 20. Partial payments are welcome at the counter, which helps an owner who is trying to shrink a balance ahead of closing day.

Mobile home bills arrive in late January and fall due April 1. If the home carries a homestead exemption, the tax for it is folded into the property bill at the end of the year, so no early mobile home bill is mailed.

The state's property tax facts page for the county says a taxpayer gets 60 days from the postmark on the bill before interest begins. It also notes that the local governing authority may move the official date. Standing timber is a one-time event: it is assessed at its whole market value when sold or harvested, and the tax goes to the commissioner of the county where the trees stood.

Before you sign a contract, ask the commissioner's staff for a payoff on your parcel in writing. Your closing attorney will need that figure.

sections.h2: What is the appeal route if a Madison County value looks too high?
sections.html:
Mail a written appeal so it is postmarked within 45 days of the date on the notice. Property Valuation refuses faxes, emails and any other electronic delivery, because it cannot confirm who sent them or what value was under appeal.

The county describes four steps. First, a letter with the parcel number, the reason and a phone number. Second, a staff review and possibly an appointment. Third, notice of a change, or an automatic move to the Board of Equalization (or arbitration, if you asked for it up front). Fourth, Superior Court for whoever is still unhappy.

  • Grounds that count: value, taxability and equalization. Complaints about the size of the bill do not.
  • The Board of Equalization is drawn from people eligible for grand jury service and charges nothing.
  • Arbitration costs each side its own arbitrator plus half of a third.
  • The court filing fee quoted by the county is $25.
  • A recent state law bars the assessors from altering a board or court result for two years unless they inspect the property or a return is filed.

The county invites recent sale information and photos of comparable homes. Skip the window and that year's appeal rights are gone.

sections.h2: What are the S and L codes on Madison County exemptions?
sections.html:
The county sorts homestead relief into letter codes. S1 means an owner-occupied principal residence, with the owner holding title to both home and land. S3 and L3 apply from age 62 with income under $10,000 for the applicant and spouse, leaving out Social Security and retirement pay. L4 starts at 65 and L5 at 70, with no income test at all.

S5 is for a veteran rated 100 percent disabled or the unremarried surviving spouse. SG is for the unremarried surviving spouse of a firefighter or peace officer killed on duty, and SS is for the unremarried surviving spouse of a service member killed in action.

File between January 1 and April 1 after owning and occupying the home on January 1. The three-member Board of Assessors meets monthly to act on homestead, conservation and preferential status requests, so a late application waits for the next cycle. Colbert has its own city exemption that you request from the town. For the other five towns, ask the city clerk whether a separate city levy exists.

Someone who buys your house has to apply in their own name, so do not count the exemption as part of what you are selling.

sections.h2: Who pays what when a Madison County house sells?
sections.html:
The county taxes whoever held title on January 1. A June closing can still leave the seller holding a December bill, which is why the contract language and the closing statement matter.

The state adds a transfer tax at recording. Georgia's revenue department sets it at $1 for the first $1,000 plus 10 cents per further $100, charges it to the seller by default, and refers questions to the Clerk of Superior Court.

Properties once sold at a Madison County tax sale may have money waiting. The Tax Commissioner posts an excess funds list and takes claims on an application form.

  • Get the payoff figure on paper ahead of closing.
  • Make sure your exemption ends once the deed records.
  • Mail your forwarding address so later notices reach you.

faqs.q: What day do Madison County property taxes come due?
faqs.a: Expect a September mailing and a normal deadline of December 20 for land, houses and business property. A mobile home has its own April 1 deadline. If the printed date on your bill differs, believe the bill.

faqs.q: Is an emailed appeal accepted in Madison County?
faqs.a: No. Madison County wants paper, mailed so the postmark lands within 45 days of the notice date. Fax and electronic submissions are turned away.

faqs.q: Which office decides what my Madison County house is worth?
faqs.a: The Board of Assessors does, with Property Valuation staff doing the fieldwork. Value is outside the Tax Commissioner's role.

faqs.q: Does a new owner keep my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. A buyer has to apply personally, with January 1 to April 1 as the window. Anything filed after April 1 first helps in the next tax year.

faqs.q: Can I pay part of a Madison County tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The commissioner's office takes installments of any size on a property bill. Request the balance in writing so you know the exact remainder at closing.
